# Witness the native titlebar drag of a popup onto another popup

## Context

#18029 (PR #18040) repaired the native-titlebar popup drag against the **main** window and left one e2e arm behind, `WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL`. The multi-window continuation — a torn-out popup moved by its OS titlebar **onto another torn-out popup** — has no witness at all: every popup-over-popup spec (`WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL`) drives the pointer path and calls `publishGeometry()` by hand. A ten-run diagnostic probe on `dev@ff4ccd512b` proved the gesture works end to end; the receipts and the rig facts are on Epic #15239 ([comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/15239#issuecomment-5500682844)). The operator asked for more e2e coverage of exactly this surface (2026-09-01).

Live latest-open sweep at 2026-09-01T21:23Z (newest #18044) plus keyword sweeps (`native titlebar vessel`, `popup over popup native`, `titlebar drag transfer vessel`): no equivalent. Nearest: #17578 (open, pointer-path coordinator gap), #16123 / #16497 (closed native-return tickets), #18029 (closed, main-window target only).

## The Problem

The class of defect #18029 exposed — a working feature silently broken because nothing exercises its trigger — applies with more force to the multi-window path, which has three more moving parts than the main-window path: the vessel participation's claim (`workstation-vessel:<item>` stable ids), the vessel-target park (`parkTearOutVessel` with a non-main target route), and the cross-window `transferItem` commit into the vessel document. None is witnessed on the native path today, so a regression in any of them would ship green.

## The Architectural Reality

- Trigger: `Neo.main.addon.WindowPosition` publishes on each movement of the source popup (poll owned by `observeMovement`, Workstation opt-in since #18040); no pointer event exists on this path.
- Claim: `DragCoordinator#onWindowPositionChange` (`src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs:1034`) → `resolveClaimedTarget` over the `workstation-cross-window` sort group; `GestureClaimArbiter` keeps hover **seniority across moves** and settles ties lexicographically, so a popup that first claims main keeps main while it still intersects main.
- Preview: `Workspace#renderCrossWindowPreview` for a vessel workspace; `ensureCrossWindowPreviewGeometry` measures asynchronously and nothing re-renders on resolve — the first update over an unmeasured target renders nothing, the next update renders.
- Terminal: dwell 450 ms / settle 250 ms → `commitNativeWindowDrop` → `suspendNativeWindowDrag` → `parkTearOutVessel({nativeTitlebar: true})` (non-main target requires `targetRoute.capabilities.focus`, granted by `Main.nativeWindowCapabilities` defaults) → `onRemoteDrop` → `commitCrossWindowTransfer` → `transferItem` into `workstation-vessel-tabs:<item>` → `retireNativeWindowDrag` closes the source vessel.
- Rig facts that decide whether a run is evidence: Playwright emulates `window.screen` at the viewport size (a popup outside the main window is then off the emulated screen and the app's `window.moveTo` cannot park it — `viewport: null` restores the real display); Chrome will not shrink the main window below ~500 px wide, so on an 800×600 stage the target sits *below* a 300 px-tall main window; the pop-outs must happen before the shrink or the tab headers collapse into the overflow menu; the source must reach the target without pausing over main.

## The Fix

Add `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL.spec.mjs` (Neural Link fixture, `viewport: null`), sibling of `WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL`:

1. Stage guard: `test.skip` when the real display cannot hold a 760 px main window plus a 240 px target below it, with the reason stated.
2. Pop out the target (`metrics`) then the source (`commits`) via the header action; after each, wait for the detach projection's refresh (main `Participation` id changes) and for all three participations to be registered.
3. Shrink the main window to 300 px tall (wait for `manager.Window` to publish it), place the target vessel fully on-screen below main, outside the main rect.
4. Assert the source realm's poll is armed by config and no `mouseout` reaches it; move the source straight onto the target's centre, then nudge twice inside the dwell window.
5. Assert, in order: the last claim is `workstation-vessel:metrics`; `.neo-dock-preview-affordance` count in the target popup ≥ 1 while the main window shows 0; `lastVesselParkReceipt.parked === true`; `lastCrossWindowTransfer` is `transferItem` `commits` → `workstation-vessel:metrics` with `applied: true`; the source vessel retires (`tearOutPanes.commits` null, popup closed); the target vessel document lists both items; the main document no longer lists `commits`; no page errors.
6. Header comment carries the trigger discipline (CDP bounds = window-server stand-in only; no synthetic input; no runtime patching) and the four rig facts.

## Decision Record impact

aligned-with ADR 0029 §2.8 (claim protocol, outcome machine, vessel lifecycle) — a witness of landed behaviour, no authority mutation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The spec exists at the path above, is green three consecutive runs at the PR head on an 800×600-or-larger real display, and skips with a stated reason on a smaller one.
- [ ] It asserts the claim, the target-realm preview, the park receipt, the `transferItem` commit, and the source retirement — each on a production receipt, none on a synthetic input.
- [ ] No pointer event and no `publishGeometry()` call reaches either popup realm during the gesture (a `mouseout` counter in the source realm is asserted at zero).
- [ ] `WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL` and `WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL` are untouched and stay green where they run.
- [ ] The spec header documents the four rig facts so the next author does not re-derive them.

## Out of Scope

- Wiring the Neural Link tier into CI (`playwright.config.e2e.mjs` gates it on the external Brain runtime; #17844 owns battery runs).
- A preview on the *first* hover over an unmeasured target (a design gap in `ensureCrossWindowPreviewGeometry`, benign under continuous movement; would be its own leaf).
- Multi-display behaviour (`window.moveTo` is unpermissioned across displays, per the D#15204 audit).

## Avoided Traps

- Emulating the screen with `test.use({screen})` — it did not take effect in this rig and would hide the `window.moveTo` clamp; `viewport: null` is the honest stage.
- Walking the source through the main window in steps — the arbiter's seniority makes main win and a pause there reintegrates into main (the feature, not a bug); the witness moves once, directly.
- Reading the preview after a single update — the measurement is asynchronous; the witness reads after the second update and inside the dwell window.
- Any synthetic `mouseout` or CDP mouse input — it would test the trigger the human gesture never produces (#18029's lesson).
